about: THE SEARCH BEHIND THE WEB SEARCH TEST (training/evaluate.mjs; training/support/search.mjs). The test offers each model a search tool and runs the searches itself, so it needs a search service behind it. Two are known. searxng, the one used where nothing else is said: SearXNG, a free metasearch engine, served on this machine for the length of the run from the revision pinned here (training/evaluate.sh installs it into .work/searxng the first time; nothing of it is in the swarm). It needs no key. serpapi: the service the test's own package was written for, which needs a key a person holds (SERPAPI_API_KEY). SWARM_SEARCH names the one to use. Either way the larger model and the swarm are asked through the same one on the same day; with searxng, what each query returned and each page fetched is kept for the day (.work/eval/search/<day>), so the two are given the same results for the same query. A score measured through one service is not to be set beside a score measured through the other.

searxng.name: SearXNG
searxng.enginesAbout: Engines turned on beside the ones SearXNG has on as it comes (measured from this project's machine 2026-11-21, six questions each, one every few seconds): Bing, Yahoo, Yandex and PrivacyWall answered every one, as DuckDuckGo and Brave did. Not turned on: Google (refused), Qwant and Fireball (access denied), Yep, Tusksearch, Baidu (errors), Mwmbl and Naver (they answer, but are a small index and a Korean one). A search is answered while any of them answers. pace: the least seconds between two searches sent out (one that is kept for the day is not sent): the engines refused when asked without one, and answered when asked every three seconds. waits: how long before each further try of a search that came back with nothing.
